docs.title: package
docs.text: package makes sure a system package is installed, or not installed. Sadame reads /etc/os-release to pick the package manager, so the same recipe works on Debian and Ubuntu (apt), Rocky, AlmaLinux and Fedora (dnf), Alpine (apk), and Arch and Arch-based systems such as Omarchy (pacman). Before acting it asks the package manager whether the package is installed, and only installs or removes when the answer differs from the recipe.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
examples/resources/package/minimal.rb
package "htop"

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description state :installed or :absent :installed Whether the package must be installed. options String or Array of Strings none Extra flags for the install or remove command, placed before the package name. A String is used as is; Array elements are each shell-quoted. notifies [:action, "type[name]"], optionally with :immediately, or a list of them none Actions to run on other resources when this one changes. See Notifications. subscribes [:action, "type[name]"], optionally with :immediately, or a list of them none Actions to run on this resource when another one changes.

docs.title: Commands per package manager
docs.text:
NAME is the package name, OPTIONS the options: value.

Manager Detected on Installed when Install Remove apt ID or ID_LIKE is debian, ubuntu dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' NAME ends in installed DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y OPTIONS NAME DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get remove -y OPTIONS NAME dnf rhel, centos, fedora, rocky, almalinux, ol rpm -q NAME exits 0 dnf install -y OPTIONS NAME dnf remove -y OPTIONS NAME apk alpine apk info -e NAME exits 0 apk add OPTIONS NAME apk del OPTIONS NAME pacman arch, archarm, manjaro, endeavouros pacman -Q NAME exits 0 pacman -S --needed --noconfirm OPTIONS NAME pacman -Rns --noconfirm OPTIONS NAME

Index refreshes:

  • apt: DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update runs once per apply, right before the first install. Runs that install nothing never touch the network.
  • dnf and apk refresh their metadata themselves.
  • pacman: sadame never runs pacman -Sy. Refreshing the sync database without upgrading (-Sy without -u) is a partial upgrade, which Arch does not support. Keep the system upgraded with pacman -Syu as usual.

docs.title: AUR packages
docs.text:
The package resource does not install from the AUR in this release. Until it does, use an AUR helper such as yay or paru through exec, guarded so it only runs when the package is missing:

examples/resources/package/aur.rb
# AUR packages are not handled by the package resource in sadame 0.1. Use an
# AUR helper through exec, guarded so it only runs when the package is
# missing and the helper is installed. yay and paru refuse to run as root,
# so the command runs as the user named in vars[:aur_user].
exec "runuser -u #{vars[:aur_user]} -- yay -S --needed --noconfirm visual-studio-code-bin",
     only_if: "command -v yay",
     not_if: "pacman -Q visual-studio-code-bin"
examples/resources/package/vars.rb
# The AUR helper must run as a normal user. When sadame runs through sudo,
# SUDO_USER is the user who called it.
{
  aur_user: ENV["SUDO_USER"] || ENV["USER"]
}

AUR helpers refuse to run as root, which is why the command goes through runuser. The helper then calls sudo pacman itself, so that user needs to be able to run pacman with sudo without a password prompt: sadame runs commands with standard input closed and cannot answer one. Without yay installed, only_if skips the resource:

$ sudo sadame plan examples/resources/package/aur.rb
sadame 0.1.0.dev plan on local (Arch Linux)

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Fresh Arch containers have no sync database. In the archlinux Docker image, pacman -S warns "database file for 'core' does not exist" and fails with "target not found" until pacman -Syu has run once. Installed systems do not have this problem.
  • Package groups and virtual packages. The installed check asks for the exact name. A group such as base-devel on Arch, or a name that is only provided by another package, never reports as installed, so it shows up in every plan. Declare the member packages instead.
  • Expecting upgrades. state: :installed means "some version is installed". Sadame does not upgrade packages in this release.
  • Mixing families without a condition. package "apache2" on Rocky fails at apply time with the package manager's own error.

docs.text:

docs.title: service
docs.text: service manages a systemd unit: whether it starts at boot (enable) and whether it is running now (state). It reads the current state with systemctl is-enabled and systemctl is-active and only calls systemctl to change what differs. Other resources can ask a service to reload or restart when they change, through notifies:.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
examples/resources/service/minimal.rb
service "nginx", enable: true, state: :running

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Type Default Description enable true or false unmanaged Start at boot (systemctl enable) or not (systemctl disable). Enabled means systemctl is-enabled prints enabled. state :running or :stopped unmanaged Running now (systemctl start) or not (systemctl stop). Running means systemctl is-active prints active. notifies [:action, "type[name]"], optionally with :immediately, or a list of them none Actions to run on other resources when this one changes. See Notifications. subscribes [:action, "type[name]"], optionally with :immediately, or a list of them none Actions to run on this resource when another one changes.

A service with neither option manages nothing by itself; it is still a valid target for notifications.

docs.title: Actions for notifications
docs.text:
Other resources can trigger these with notifies: [:action, "service[name]"]:

Action Runs :start systemctl start NAME :stop systemctl stop NAME :restart systemctl restart NAME :reload systemctl reload NAME :enable systemctl enable NAME :disable systemctl disable NAME

Actions run only when the notifying resource changed. By default they run once each, after all resources; add :immediately to run one right away. See the scenario below and Notifications.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
examples/resources/service/recipe.rb
# On Arch, installing nginx does not enable or start it; the service
# resource does. Debian and Ubuntu start services on install, so there the
# same resource usually reports no change.
package "nginx"
service "nginx", enable: true, state: :running

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• No systemd. The resource needs a running systemd (it checks for /run/systemd/system). In containers without systemd, and on Alpine with OpenRC, it fails with "systemd is not running on this host".
  • Declaring the service before its package. On a fresh machine the unit does not exist yet, so plan shows it as disabled and stopped, and apply fails if the package comes later in the recipe. Put package first.
  • Units that cannot be enabled. systemctl is-enabled prints static for units without an [Install] section. Those never count as enabled, so enable: true on them shows a change on every plan. Leave enable out.
  • Expecting a reload when only the service changed. reload and restart happen only through notifications from other resources.
  • Reloading a service that cannot reload. systemctl reload fails for units without ExecReload=. Notify :restart for those.

docs.title: user
docs.text: user manages a local Linux user account: whether it exists, its UID, home directory, login shell, and the groups it must belong to. It reads the account with getent passwd and id -nG, and changes it with useradd, usermod and userdel only when something differs.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
examples/resources/user/minimal.rb
user "deploy"

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Type Default Description uid Integer unmanaged Numeric user ID. home String unmanaged Home directory path. shell String unmanaged Login shell, such as "/bin/bash" or "/usr/sbin/nologin". groups Array of Strings unmanaged Groups the user must belong to. Other memberships are left alone. The groups must exist. system true or false false Create a system account (useradd -r), which gets no home directory. Only used when the user is created. state :present or :absent :present :absent deletes the account with userdel; the home directory is kept. notifies [:action, "type[name]"], optionally with :immediately, or a list of them none Actions to run on other resources when this one changes. See Notifications. subscribes [:action, "type[name]"], optionally with :immediately, or a list of them none Actions to run on this resource when another one changes.

New users that are not system users get a home directory (useradd -m). Changing home on an existing user updates the account but does not move files.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Groups that do not exist yet. useradd -G docker fails if the docker group has not been created. Declare the package that creates it first.
  • Alpine without shadow. Alpine's BusyBox has no useradd. Declare package "shadow" before any user resource; without it the resource fails with a message saying so.
  • Expecting a group list to be exact. Removing a group from groups: does not remove the user from that group.
  • Clashing with existing accounts. Many distributions ship system users such as backup or www-data. Declaring one of those with a different home or shell changes the existing account.
